title: VESIT Green Campus Sustainability Policy 2024-2040
content:
VESIT GREEN CAMPUS SUSTAINABILITY POLICY (2024-2040)
Document Reference: VESIT/POL/ENV/2024/V1
Institution: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
Promulgated by: The Governing Board, Academic Council, and the Campus Sustainability Taskforce.

1. EXECUTIVE MANDATE AND STRATEGIC VISION
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), situated in Chembur, Mumbai, formally commits to achieving institutional net-zero operational greenhouse gas emissions by December 31, 2040. As an apex engineering and higher education institution serving over 3,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students alongside 200 faculty and administrative staff across a built-up area of 32,500 m2, the college recognizes that educational institutions must lead by example in practical environmental decarbonisation. This statutory charter establishes binding decarbonisation trajectories, departmental obligations, technological pathways, and continuous monitoring mechanisms governed by the interactive EcoClock AI platform.

The policy is deliberately anchored in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), establishing verified operational linkages with SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

2. JURISDICTIONAL SCOPE AND PHYSICAL BOUNDARIES
This policy exercises mandatory operational jurisdiction over all physical real estate, utility infrastructure, and operational workflows encompassing:
- Academic Block A (BLD_ACA, 7,500 m2, occupancy 1,100), housing the Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN) and Department of Electronics & Telecommunication (DEP_EXTC).
- Academic Block B (BLD_ACB, 6,800 m2, occupancy 950), accommodating the Department of Information Technology (DEP_INFT).
- Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB, 5,200 m2, occupancy 650), housing the Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS) and high-density computing clusters.
- Library (BLD_LIB, 3,100 m2, occupancy 350), housing print collections and digital repository archives.
- Auditorium (BLD_AUD, 2,800 m2, seating capacity 800), dedicated to institutional conferences and cultural symposia.
- Canteen (BLD_CAN, 2,100 m2, occupancy 400), serving over 2,200 daily meals and snacks.
- Administration Block (BLD_ADM, 5,000 m2, occupancy 200), housing the Principal's Directorate, Finance, and Campus Facilities (DEP_ADMN).

3. QUANTIFIED STRATEGIC TARGETS AND DECARBONISATION BENCHMARKS
The Governing Board mandates five foundational quantitative targets to guide institutional operational investments between baseline year 2024 and 2040:
3.1 Target Net-Zero (TRG_NET_ZERO): Abate the institutional carbon baseline of 2,450,000 kg CO2e (2,450 metric tonnes CO2e/year) to absolute net-zero by December 31, 2040. The abatement pathway mandates a steady reduction of at least 153,125 kg CO2e annually across Scope 1 direct diesel emissions, Scope 2 indirect grid electricity emissions, and Scope 3 commuter transport and landfill waste emissions.
3.2 Target Renewable Penetration (TRG_RENEWABLE): Scale campus clean electricity generation from the 2024 baseline of 14.8% (312,400 kWh/year) to a minimum of 50.0% renewable electricity penetration by December 31, 2030, through on-site rooftop solar photovoltaic generation and green power wheeling agreements.
3.3 Target Zero Waste to Landfill (TRG_ZERO_WASTE): Escalate solid waste diversion from municipal dump sites from 42.0% to 85.0% by December 31, 2028, deploying mandatory source segregation, aerobic composting, and authorized e-waste recovery.
3.4 Target Water Neutrality (TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL): Curtail annual municipal piped water demand by 30.0% relative to the 2024 baseline of 48,000,000 litres, reducing gross intake to 33,600,000 litres/year by 2029 through integrated rainwater harvesting and greywater recycling.
3.5 Target Green Commuting (TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE): Increase low-carbon commuter modal share from 52.0% to 70.0% of all passenger-kilometres by 2027 by incentivizing suburban rail transit, municipal electric buses, non-motorized cycling, and dedicated campus feeder transit.

4. INSTITUTIONAL INITIATIVES AND ACTION FRAMEWORKS
To operationalize these binding targets, the institution has chartered seven interdisciplinary initiatives:
- INIT_SOLAR_PH1 (Phase-1 Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic Grid-Tied Project): 220 kWp installed monocrystalline arrays across BLD_ACA (80 kWp), BLD_ACB (70 kWp), BLD_LIB (30 kWp), and BLD_ADM (40 kWp), generating 312,400 kWh/year and abating 256,168 kg CO2e.
- INIT_SOLAR_PH2 (Phase-2 Solar Expansion & Battery Storage Proposal): 150 kWp parking canopy arrays and 50 kWp bifacial PV modules on BLD_AUD paired with a 100 kWh LiFePO4 battery energy storage system (BESS) delivering 284,000 kWh/year and avoiding 232,880 kg CO2e.
- INIT_RWH_SYSTEM (Integrated Rainwater Harvesting & Groundwater Recharge): Intercepting 18,000 m2 of terrace catchments across BLD_ACA, BLD_ACB, and BLD_LIB with 450,000 litres of filtration cistern capacity, capturing 12,400,000 litres annually.
- INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN (Smart Food Waste Digester & Organic Aerobic Composting Pit): A 250 kg/day biomethanation digester at BLD_CAN displacing 14 commercial LPG cylinders monthly and abating 48,000 kg CO2e.
- INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE (Zero-Emission Electric Campus Transit & Station Feeder Van): Dedicated electric shuttle vans operating between Chembur/Kurla railway stations and the campus gate, mitigating 36,000 kg CO2e annually.
- INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT (Campus-Wide IoT Smart Sub-Metering & Energy Audit Protocol): 45 Modbus-RS485 digital energy meters and edge gateways across seven campus blocks eliminating 98,000 kWh of idle nocturnal baseloads.
- INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE (Miyawaki Urban Native Afforestation & Campus Biodiversity Arboretum): A 600 m2 high-density micro-forest behind BLD_AUD comprising 1,200 native trees sequestering 14,000 kg CO2e/year.

5. GOVERNANCE, VERIFICATION, AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE
The Campus Sustainability Taskforce, chaired by the Principal and including the Heads of Department of Computer Engineering (Dr. N. Joshi), Information Technology (Dr. S. Nair), Electronics & Telecommunication (Dr. R. Kulkarni), Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (Dr. P. Sharma), and Facilities Director (Mr. V. Deshmukh), shall convene quarterly to audit utility telemetry, verify carbon accounting against documented emission factors (EF_ELEC_GRID 0.82 kg CO2e/kWh and EF_DIESEL_GEN 2.68 kg CO2e/L), and validate compliance with Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) norms. Full transparency shall be sustained through automated Neo4j property knowledge graph indexing and public-facing visual telemetry.

title: Comprehensive Campus Environmental and Carbon Audit Report 2024
content:
COMPREHENSIVE CAMPUS ENVIRONMENTAL AND CARBON AUDIT REPORT 2024
Document Reference: VESIT/AUD/GHG/2024/01
Conducting Authority: Bureau of Energy and Carbon Verification in coordination with VESIT Campus Sustainability Taskforce.
Audited Entity: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY AND AUDIT METHODOLOGY
An exhaustive calendar year 2024 baseline greenhouse gas (GHG) and utility audit was conducted across the 32,500 m2 built-up campus of Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) in Chembur, Mumbai. The accounting methodology adheres rigorously to the GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard and ISO 14064-1 specifications. The audit quantified Scope 1 direct emissions, Scope 2 indirect emissions from imported electricity, and material Scope 3 value-chain emissions generated across seven principal facilities: Academic Block A (BLD_ACA), Academic Block B (BLD_ACB), Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB), Library (BLD_LIB), Auditorium (BLD_AUD), Canteen (BLD_CAN), and Administration Block (BLD_ADM).

The verified institutional carbon footprint for calendar year 2024 stands at exactly 2,450,000 kg CO2e (2,450.00 metric tonnes CO2e), establishing the baseline against which the campus net-zero target (TRG_NET_ZERO) for December 31, 2040, is statutorily benchmarked.

2. EMISSION SOURCE ATTRIBUTION AND ACTIVITY INVENTORY
2.1 Scope 1 (Direct Combustion Emissions):
Direct emissions are predominantly generated by stationary diesel generator sets (DG) deployed for emergency electrical backup during regional grid outages. In 2024, emergency generators consumed 18,400 litres of low-sulfur high-speed diesel fuel. Applying documented IPCC Emission Factor EF_DIESEL_GEN (2.68 kg CO2e/litre), Scope 1 emissions totaled 49,312 kg CO2e (2.01% of gross institutional emissions). An additional 1,200 kg CO2e was generated from minor liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) usage in academic laboratories.
2.2 Scope 2 (Indirect Emissions from Purchased Grid Electricity):
Campus electricity importation from the Maharashtra State regional grid totaled 2,050,000 kWh in 2024. In accordance with Central Electricity Authority (CEA) Baseline Database Version 19.0 (Emission Factor EF_ELEC_GRID = 0.82 kg CO2e/kWh), imported electricity accounted for 1,681,000 kg CO2e (68.61% of total emissions). On-site rooftop solar photovoltaic generation under INIT_SOLAR_PH1 supplied an additional 312,400 kWh of zero-carbon power, preventing 256,168 kg CO2e of additional grid emissions. Total campus electrical consumption reached 2,362,400 kWh, establishing a 13.22% clean electricity penetration rate.
2.3 Scope 3 (Indirect Value Chain and Municipal Emissions):
Scope 3 emissions totaled 719,688 kg CO2e (29.38% of total emissions):
- Commuter Transportation: Commuting across 3,000 students and 200 staff generated 580,000 kg CO2e. Modal analysis indicates that private passenger cars generated 165,300 kg CO2e (EF_TRANS_CAR = 0.175 kg CO2e/pkm), two-wheelers generated 111,940 kg CO2e (EF_TRANS_BIKE = 0.042 kg CO2e/pkm), municipal buses generated 152,000 kg CO2e (EF_TRANS_BUS = 0.054 kg CO2e/pkm), and suburban electric trains produced 150,760 kg CO2e (EF_TRANS_TRAIN = 0.028 kg CO2e/pkm).
- Solid Waste Disposal: Municipal solid waste delivered to Deonar landfill contributed 115,000 kg CO2e based on factor EF_WASTE_LANDFILL (1.25 kg CO2e/kg waste).
- Embodied Water Treatment: Municipal pumping and wastewater processing for 48,000,000 litres accounted for 24,688 kg CO2e.

3. BUILDING-SPECIFIC ENERGY AND EMISSIONS BENCHMARKING
- Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB, 5,200 m2): Registered the highest electricity intensity at 112 kWh/m2/year (annual total 582,400 kWh), driven by 16 computer labs, 2 primary server rooms, and continuous air conditioning.
- Academic Block A (BLD_ACA, 7,500 m2): Consumed 382,500 kWh (51.0 kWh/m2/year). Rooftop solar generated 113,600 kWh, supplying 29.7% of building demand.
- Academic Block B (BLD_ACB, 6,800 m2): Consumed 333,200 kWh (49.0 kWh/m2/year). Rooftop solar supplied 99,400 kWh (29.8% solar fraction).
- Administration Block (BLD_ADM, 5,000 m2): Consumed 228,000 kWh (45.6 kWh/m2/year), offset by 56,800 kWh of solar generation.
- Library (BLD_LIB, 3,100 m2): Consumed 168,200 kWh (54.2 kWh/m2/year), with 42,600 kWh provided by rooftop solar PV.
- Auditorium (BLD_AUD, 2,800 m2): Consumed 134,200 kWh (47.9 kWh/m2/year), characterized by sharp intermittent event cooling peaks.
- Canteen (BLD_CAN, 2,100 m2): Consumed 192,000 kWh (91.4 kWh/m2/year) alongside substantial thermal and water usage.

4. TARGET TRACKING AND STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATIONS
The audit benchmarks progress against institutional targets: TRG_NET_ZERO requires linear annual abatement of 153,125 kg CO2e; TRG_RENEWABLE mandates expanding clean energy from 14.8% to 50.0% by 2030; TRG_ZERO_WASTE demands diverting 85% of waste from landfills by 2028; and TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL requires a 30% reduction in municipal water intake by 2029. Immediate auditor recommendations mandate executing Phase-2 Solar (INIT_SOLAR_PH2) on BLD_AUD and parking canopies, deploying variable refrigerant flow chillers in BLD_LAB, expanding the electric shuttle (INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE), and scaling Canteen composting (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN) to support SDG 7, SDG 11, SDG 12, and SDG 13.

title: Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic Performance Assessment: Phase 1
content:
ROOFTOP SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT: PHASE 1
Document Reference: VESIT/ENG/SOLAR/2024/01
Project Reference: INIT_SOLAR_PH1 (Phase-1 Rooftop Solar PV Project)
Executing Departments: Department of Electronics & Telecommunication (DEP_EXTC) and Campus Facilities (DEP_ADMN).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
The Phase-1 Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic (PV) installation (INIT_SOLAR_PH1) was commissioned in November 2023 under net-metering regulations established by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) in partnership with the local utility distribution licensee (Adani Electricity Mumbai Limited / BEST). The grid-tied solar system comprises a rated DC capacity of 220 kWp utilizing Tier-1 high-efficiency monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic modules (400 Wp rated output per panel, 20.8% module conversion efficiency) coupled with commercial three-phase string solar inverters.

The 220 kWp total capacity is distributed across four institutional building terraces:
- Academic Block A (BLD_ACA): 80 kWp DC capacity (200 modules of 400 Wp), coupled with two 40 kW string inverters.
- Academic Block B (BLD_ACB): 70 kWp DC capacity (175 modules), coupled with one 50 kW and one 20 kW inverter.
- Administration Block (BLD_ADM): 40 kWp DC capacity (100 modules), connected to one 40 kW inverter.
- Library (BLD_LIB): 30 kWp DC capacity (75 modules), connected to one 30 kW inverter.

All arrays are mounted on elevated hot-dip galvanized structural steel pergolas tilted at a fixed 19° south-facing azimuth, optimized for Mumbai's geographic latitude (19.0760° N) to maximize annual solar irradiance capture while providing unimpeded pedestrian access on terrace roofs.

2. ANNUAL GENERATION PERFORMANCE AND SEASONAL DYNAMICS
Throughout the 12-month evaluation cycle from July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024, the 220 kWp solar PV system generated a verified gross total of 312,400 kWh of clean electricity:
- Quarter 1 (July - September): Generated 52,600 kWh. The southwest monsoon created dense overcast cloud cover and heavy rainfall, causing monthly generation to drop to seasonal lows of 14,200 kWh in July and 15,800 kWh in August.
- Quarter 2 (October - December): Generated 82,400 kWh as clear post-monsoon skies and moderate ambient temperatures restored monthly yields to 27,200 kWh.
- Quarter 3 (January - March): Generated 93,600 kWh, benefiting from high atmospheric transparency and optimal solar irradiance in Chembur.
- Quarter 4 (April - June): Generated 83,800 kWh. Peak monthly generation occurred in April, reaching 32,800 kWh, before late-May pre-monsoon cloudiness emerged.

Building-level solar contributions were: BLD_ACA produced 113,600 kWh; BLD_ACB produced 99,400 kWh; BLD_ADM produced 56,800 kWh; and BLD_LIB generated 42,600 kWh. Specific plant performance ratio (PR) averaged 78.4% over the annual cycle, comfortably exceeding the guaranteed contractual threshold of 75.0%.

3. ENVIRONMENTAL DECARBONISATION AND FINANCIAL AUDIT
By generating 312,400 kWh of on-site solar power, the college avoided importing an equivalent volume of fossil-intensive grid electricity from the Western Regional Grid. Applying the Central Electricity Authority baseline grid factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh), the Phase-1 solar installation prevented exactly 256,168 kg CO2e (256.17 metric tonnes CO2e) of indirect Scope 2 emissions in 2024.

Financial analysis confirms commercial viability:
- Total Displaced Grid Electricity Value: At an average institutional commercial tariff of INR 11.00 per kWh, annual gross electricity bill savings equaled INR 34,36,400 (34.36 Lakhs).
- Operation and Maintenance Costs: Annual preventive servicing, robotic cleaning, and inverter monitoring totaled INR 2,80,000.
- Net Annual Financial Savings: INR 31,56,400.
- Capital Payback Horizon: Against a turnkey installation expenditure of INR 1.32 Crores, the realized simple payback period is exactly 4.18 years, delivering robust return on investment while advancing institutional target TRG_RENEWABLE and supporting SDG 7, SDG 11, and SDG 13.

4. MAINTENANCE REGIME AND SOILING DEGRADATION ANALYSIS
Telemetry from IoT sub-meters installed under INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT revealed that urban particulate accumulation from Mumbai traffic and industrial activity in Chembur causes substantial soiling loss. Unwashed arrays experienced a measured 12.4% degradation in daily power yield over a three-week dry period in January 2024. Consequently, a bi-weekly automated water cleaning protocol utilizing harvested rainwater from INIT_RWH_SYSTEM was established, recovering 10.8% of lost yield. Recommendations emphasize executing the Phase-2 200 kWp expansion (INIT_SOLAR_PH2) across BLD_AUD and parking zones to achieve target TRG_RENEWABLE (50% clean electricity by 2030).

title: Phase-2 Solar Canopy and Energy Storage Feasibility Study
content:
FEASIBILITY STUDY: PHASE-2 SOLAR CANOPY AND ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM
Document Reference: VESIT/FS/SOLAR-BESS/2024/02
Project Code: INIT_SOLAR_PH2
Commissioned by: Campus Decarbonization Taskforce and Governing Board.
Technical Consultants: Department of Electronics & Telecommunication (DEP_EXTC) and Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. EXECUTIVE RATIONALE AND DECARBONISATION TARGET ALIGNMENT
To sustain compliance with the institutional Net-Zero Roadmap (TRG_NET_ZERO) by 2040 and achieve the mandatory milestone of 50.0% renewable electricity penetration by 2030 (TRG_RENEWABLE), Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) must aggressively expand clean energy generation beyond existing terrace allocations. The 220 kWp Phase-1 installation (INIT_SOLAR_PH1) currently generates 312,400 kWh/year, satisfying 13.22% of gross campus electricity demand (2,362,400 kWh). However, building terraces across Academic Block A (BLD_ACA), Academic Block B (BLD_ACB), Administration Block (BLD_ADM), and Library (BLD_LIB) have reached maximum structural weight allowances.

This engineering study evaluates the technical and financial feasibility of Project INIT_SOLAR_PH2, proposing a 200 kWp solar PV expansion combined with a 100 kWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) deployed across ground parking surfaces and the Auditorium roof (BLD_AUD), advancing SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

2. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND CIVIL-STRUCTURAL DESIGN
The proposed 200 kWp addition consists of two interconnected subsystems:
2.1 Central Parking Elevated Solar Canopy (150 kWp DC):
Installation of cantilevered structural steel canopies over the central two-wheeler and four-wheeler paved parking lots covering 1,850 m2 of surface area. The canopy will support 375 high-efficiency bifacial monocrystalline silicon modules (400 Wp each). Bifacial architecture captures direct downward solar irradiance as well as ground-reflected albedo from light-colored concrete pavers, yielding an estimated 8.5% bifacial boost. The canopy provides covered, shaded parking for 240 two-wheelers and 45 four-wheelers, integrating two Level-2 22 kW EV fast chargers for campus feeder transit (INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE).
2.2 Auditorium Perimeter Rooftop Array (50 kWp DC):
Placement of 125 bifacial 400 Wp PV modules on custom aluminum ballasted racking over the curved perimeter roof of the Auditorium (BLD_AUD, 2,800 m2), connecting directly to the BLD_AUD electrical distribution sub-board.
2.3 Battery Energy Storage System (100 kWh BESS):
A central containerized lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery system with 100 kWh nominal storage capacity and 50 kW continuous bi-directional inverter capability. LiFePO4 chemistry guarantees thermal stability in Mumbai's sub-tropical climate, delivering over 4,500 charge cycles at 80% depth of discharge.

3. ENERGY YIELD, GRID DISPLACEMENT, AND EMISSION ABATEMENT
PVSyst hydrological and solar simulation modeling calibrated with Mumbai solar irradiance datasets predicts an annual yield of 284,000 kWh for the 200 kWp Phase-2 arrays:
- Canopy Array (150 kWp): Generates 213,000 kWh/year.
- Auditorium Array (50 kWp): Generates 71,000 kWh/year.
When combined with Phase 1 (312,400 kWh), total institutional solar generation will reach 596,400 kWh/year, meeting 25.25% of total campus electrical consumption. Applying the CEA grid emission factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh), the Phase-2 system will prevent 232,880 kg CO2e of Scope 2 emissions annually. The combined solar installations will avoid 489,048 kg CO2e every year.

4. DIESEL GENERATOR ABATEMENT AND PEAK LOAD SHAVING
The integration of the 100 kWh BESS provides high-impact operational decarbonisation:
- Peak Demand Management: Discharges 45 kWh daily during high-tariff evening hours (18:00 to 21:00) during postgraduate sessions, reducing contractual peak demand penalties by INR 2,40,000 annually.
- Emergency Backup & Diesel Abatement: The BESS offers sub-20ms uninterruptible transfer capability, shielding mission-critical server rooms in the Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB) during instantaneous grid dropouts. This capability eliminates 45 hours of idling run-time on campus diesel generators, preventing the combustion of 2,400 litres of diesel fuel annually. Applying factor EF_DIESEL_GEN (2.68 kg CO2e/L), this eliminates 6,432 kg CO2e of direct Scope 1 emissions every year.

5. CAPITAL EXPENDITURE AND FINANCIAL APPRAISAL
- Total Turnkey Capital Expenditure (EPC): INR 1,48,00,000 (1.48 Crores), covering solar arrays, parking steelworks, BESS container, and grid tie-in.
- Annual Energy Savings: INR 31,24,000 (from 284,000 kWh at INR 11.00/kWh).
- Peak Demand and Diesel Fuel Savings: INR 4,81,600 (diesel savings of 2,400 L at INR 100.67/L + demand tariff cuts).
- Annual Net Operational Cashflow: INR 33,55,600 (net of O&M).
- Simple Payback Period: 4.41 years; Internal Rate of Return (IRR): 19.8% over a 25-year asset lifecycle.
The study conclusively advises immediate Board authorization and tendering.

title: Campus Water Audit and Conservation Strategy Report 2024
content:
CAMPUS WATER AUDIT AND CONSERVATION STRATEGY REPORT 2024
Document Reference: VESIT/AUD/WATER/2024/01
Conducting Cell: Environmental Civil Infrastructure Cell in collaboration with Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS).
Facility Scope: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY AND STATUTORY CONTEXT
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) encompasses 32,500 m2 of built infrastructure serving a daily population of 3,200 individuals (3,000 students and 200 faculty and administrative staff). In calendar year 2024, the institution conducted a rigorous, meter-level water balance audit across all seven campus buildings: Academic Block A (BLD_ACA), Academic Block B (BLD_ACB), Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB), Library (BLD_LIB), Auditorium (BLD_AUD), Canteen (BLD_CAN), and Administration Block (BLD_ADM).

The audit established that gross annual freshwater intake from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) utility supply reached 48,000,000 litres (48,000 m3). Daily consumption averages 131,500 litres during active semester instruction days. The findings benchmark institutional target TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL, which legally binds the college to curtail municipal piped water demand by 30.0% (saving 14,400,000 litres annually to reach a ceiling of 33,600,000 litres) by 2029, in strict alignment with United Nations SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

2. END-USE WATER CONSUMPTION BREAKDOWN
Detailed telemetry and fixture log analysis identifies four predominant consumption centers:
2.1 Restrooms, Urinals, and Sanitation Hygiene (46.0% - 22,080,000 litres/year):
Sanitary plumbing across BLD_ACA, BLD_ACB, and BLD_LAB represents the largest campus water draw, consuming an average of 60,500 litres per working day. Conventional flush tanks discharging 10-12 litres per cycle and untuned push-button washbasin taps discharging 9.0 litres/minute account for substantial wastage.
2.2 Canteen and Catering Culinary Facilities (28.0% - 13,440,000 litres/year):
The Canteen building (BLD_CAN) prepares over 2,200 meals and snacks daily. Primary water uses include industrial dishwashing, cooking, utensil pre-rinsing, and reverse osmosis (RO) drinking water purification. Commercial RO purifiers currently exhibit a 65% brine reject rate, discharging approximately 14,000 litres of clean reject water into municipal drains daily.
2.3 Botanical Landscaping and Grounds Irrigation (18.0% - 8,640,000 litres/year):
Maintenance of campus lawns, peripheral tree groves, and the 600 m2 high-density Miyawaki micro-forest (INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE) behind BLD_AUD requires 23,600 litres/day during dry seasons (October through May), currently drawn from municipal tap supply.
2.4 Laboratory Facilities, HVAC Cooling Towers, and Janitorial Cleaning (8.0% - 3,840,000 litres/year):
Includes chemistry preparation, wet lab rinsing, chiller plant cooling tower evaporation makeup, and daily scrubbing of academic corridors.

3. PERFORMANCE OF INTEGRATED RAINWATER HARVESTING SYSTEM (INIT_RWH_SYSTEM)
Under initiative INIT_RWH_SYSTEM, the campus intercepts monsoon precipitation from 18,000 m2 of reinforced concrete terrace catchments across Academic Block A, Academic Block B, and the Library. Runoff is gravity-channeled through leaf screens and multi-media sand-gravel bed filtration units into three underground reinforced concrete storage cisterns with a combined capacity of 450,000 litres.

During the 2024 monsoon season (June to September), Mumbai received 2,420 mm of precipitation. The harvesting system successfully captured, filtered, and utilized 12,400,000 litres of rainwater, directly displacing 25.83% of annual municipal freshwater demand. Harvested rainwater was pumped to dual-plumbing overhead tanks for toilet flushing in BLD_ACA and BLD_ACB, and for cooling tower replenishment. An additional 26,800,000 litres of surplus terrace runoff was routed into four deep injection borewells, recharging the regional coastal aquifer table and preventing urban storm flooding.

4. ACTION PLAN FOR WATER REDUCTION (TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL)
To achieve the mandated 30% reduction by 2029, the Environmental Infrastructure Cell mandates three capital interventions:
- Comprehensive Aerator Fixture Retrofit: Install pressure-compensating multi-stream aerators on 140 washroom faucets across all academic blocks, restricting flow rates from 9.0 L/min to 3.5 L/min. Projected annual savings: 3,500,000 litres.
- Reverse Osmosis Reject Water Redirection: Plumb the 14,000 L/day RO purification reject line directly into the toilet flushing cisterns of BLD_CAN and BLD_ACA. Projected savings: 3,640,000 litres/year.
- Greywater Reed-Bed Biofilter Upgrade: Construct a decentralized 15,000 L/day horizontal subsurface flow constructed wetland adjacent to BLD_CAN, treating kitchen sink greywater to non-potable standards for landscape and Miyawaki forest irrigation. Projected savings: 3,900,000 litres/year.
Combined savings total 11,040,000 litres annually, ensuring complete fulfillment of TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL.

title: Solid Waste Management and Decentralized Composting Audit 2024
content:
SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT AND DECENTRALIZED COMPOSTING AUDIT 2024
Document Reference: VESIT/AUD/WASTE/2024/01
Authoring Body: Campus Environmental Sanitation Committee and Nature Club.
Audited Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. QUANTITATIVE WASTE GENERATION PROFILE
An intensive institutional waste composition and mass-balance audit was conducted across the 32,500 m2 campus of Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) during academic year 2024. Serving a campus community of 3,200 individuals, the institution generated a total of 68,400 kg (68.40 metric tonnes) of solid municipal and electronic waste.

Characterization across 12 sampling cycles established the following waste composition breakdown:
- Organic and Kitchen Waste: 42.0% (28,728 kg/year), generated primarily by Canteen dining (BLD_CAN), food preparation peelings, leftover student meals, and botanical landscape trimmings.
- Recyclable Paper, Cardboard, and Stationeries: 33.0% (22,572 kg/year), originating from examination booklets, administrative archives, packaging crates, and Library (BLD_LIB) periodicals.
- Post-Consumer Plastics and Multi-Layer Packaging: 14.0% (9,576 kg/year), comprising beverage containers, snack wrappers, and packaging films.
- Electronic Waste (E-Waste) and Laboratory Scrap: 3.0% (2,052 kg/year), consisting of obsolete motherboard PCBs, power supplies, CRT/TFT monitors, lab wiring, and spent batteries from Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB).
- Non-Recyclable Inert and Sanitary Refuse: 8.0% (5,472 kg/year), including dust, sweepings, and sanitary bathroom waste.

2. PERFORMANCE OF DECENTRALIZED ORGANIC TREATMENT (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN)
To address the primary organic waste fraction, VESIT commissioned project INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN behind the Canteen building. The installation comprises:
- An anaerobic biomethanation plant designed with a rated processing capacity of 250 kg of organic waste per day.
- Twin 500-litre dual-axis aerobic composting tumblers with mechanical aeration for horticultural dry leaves and cellulosic paper napkins.

In calendar year 2024, the biomethanation digester successfully ingested and processed 19,200 kg of canteen wet food scraps. The anaerobic digestion process generated an average of 12 m3 of methane-rich biogas daily. This fuel is piped via stainless steel conduits directly into the commercial Canteen kitchen to supply two heavy-duty cooking burners, displacing 14 commercial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders (19 kg each) per month.

Environmental and carbon accounting confirms that diverting 19,200 kg of putrescible organic waste away from the municipal Deonar open landfill prevented uncontrolled anaerobic decomposition and fugitive methane venting. Utilizing emission factor EF_WASTE_LANDFILL (1.25 kg CO2e/kg waste) versus composting factor EF_WASTE_COMPOST (0.08 kg CO2e/kg waste), the composting and biogas plant achieved a net carbon abatement of 22,464 kg CO2e in 2024. Furthermore, the digester generated 1,400 kg of nutrient-dense organic bioslurry and bio-compost, utilized across the 600 m2 Miyawaki native forest (INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE) and campus botanical beds, eliminating synthetic chemical fertilizers.

3. DRY RECYCLABLES RECOVERY AND AUTHORIZED E-WASTE PARTNERSHIPS
Under the campus Circular Economy protocol, segregated dry paper and cardboard (22,572 kg) were sorted in the central sorting yard. Through formal tie-ups with municipal recyclers, 19,800 kg of post-consumer paper was recovered for pulping. Applying avoided paper production factor EF_WASTE_RECYCLE (-0.65 kg CO2e/kg waste), paper recovery yielded an avoided carbon credit of -12,870 kg CO2e.

Electronic waste disposal is governed by the national E-Waste Management Rules 2022. VESIT entered into a formal memorandum with authorized e-waste recycler Greenscape Solutions. During 2024, 1,850 kg of decommissioned computer electronics from BLD_LAB and DEP_CMPN underwent certified downstream material extraction, recovering precious copper, gold, aluminum, and rare earths while preventing hazardous heavy metal contamination (cadmium, lead) of Mumbai groundwaters, directly supporting United Nations SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

4. PROGRESS TOWARD TARGET TRG_ZERO_WASTE
In 2024, the institution attained an aggregate solid waste diversion rate of 48.2% (composting + formal recycling). This represents measurable progress toward target TRG_ZERO_WASTE, which mandates achieving an 85.0% diversion rate and zero organic waste to landfill by December 31, 2028. Key measures for 2025 include expanding student cafeteria plate-waste audits and enforcing a total prohibition on single-use plastics.

title: Comprehensive Campus Commuter Mobility and Transportation Survey 2024
content:
COMPREHENSIVE CAMPUS COMMUTER MOBILITY AND TRANSPORTATION SURVEY 2024
Document Reference: VESIT/SRV/MOBILITY/2024/01
Supervising Department: Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS) in collaboration with VESIT Student Council.
Target Population: 3,000 undergraduate/postgraduate students and 200 faculty and administrative staff.
Sample Universe: 2,140 verified student respondents and 172 faculty/staff respondents.
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. SURVEY METHODOLOGY AND DEMOGRAPHIC PROFILE
In February and March 2024, the Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS) deployed an exhaustive digital mobility survey across the campus community of Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus). The objective was to construct a rigorous commuter travel model, calculate Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions, and establish baseline indicators for institutional target TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE (70.0% low-carbon commuting share by 2027) supporting United Nations SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

The surveyed sample encompassed 2,312 validated respondents across all engineering departments—Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN), Information Technology (DEP_INFT), Electronics & Telecommunication (DEP_EXTC), AI & Data Science (DEP_AIDS), and Campus Administration (DEP_ADMN).

2. COMMUTER MODAL SPLIT AND DISTANCE DYNAMICS
Cross-tabulation of daily commute journeys across 22 working days per month revealed the following modal split:
- Suburban Electric Rail (48.0% of commuter trips): Represents the backbone of student transit, utilizing the Mumbai Suburban Railway Network (Harbour Line via Chembur and Tilak Nagar stations, and Central Line via Kurla station). Average one-way distance: 14.0 km (return trip: 28.0 km).
- BEST Municipal Transit Buses (22.0% of trips): Municipal electric and CNG bus networks operated by Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST), serving commuters across eastern and central Mumbai suburbs. Average one-way distance: 7.0 km (return: 14.0 km).
- Two-Wheelers (Petrol Motorcycles and Scooters) (16.0% of trips): Predominantly upper-year students and junior staff commuting from neighboring Chembur, Ghatkopar, and Sion suburbs. Average one-way distance: 6.0 km (return: 12.0 km).
- Private Passenger Motorcars (Single-Occupant and Carpools) (6.0% of trips): Predominantly senior faculty, administrative directors, and carpooling student cohorts. Average one-way distance: 9.0 km (return: 18.0 km).
- Non-Motorized Transport (Walking and Cycling) (8.0% of trips): Local students and staff residing within a 2.0 km radius of the Chembur campus. Average one-way distance: 1.0 km (return: 2.0 km).

3. TRANSPORT EMISSIONS ATTRIBUTION AND MODAL CARBON INTENSITY
Commuter mobility generates approximately 580,000 kg CO2e annually, representing 23.67% of the total institutional carbon footprint of 2,450,000 kg CO2e.
Applying verified regional emission factors:
- Private Passenger Cars: Despite representing only 6.0% of passenger trips, cars generate 165,300 kg CO2e (28.50% of transportation emissions) due to high specific carbon intensity (EF_TRANS_CAR = 0.175 kg CO2e/passenger-km).
- Two-Wheelers: Motorcycles and scooters produce 111,940 kg CO2e (19.30% of transport total) based on emission factor EF_TRANS_BIKE (0.042 kg CO2e/passenger-km).
- Municipal Buses: Produce 152,000 kg CO2e based on factor EF_TRANS_BUS (0.054 kg CO2e/passenger-km).
- Suburban Electric Trains: Account for the highest passenger-kilometres (over 5.3 million pkm) while generating only 150,760 kg CO2e due to the clean operational efficiency of electric mass transit (EF_TRANS_TRAIN = 0.028 kg CO2e/passenger-km).
- Walking and Cycling: Zero carbon emissions (0.0 kg CO2e).

4. IMPACT EVALUATION OF CAMPUS ELECTRIC SHUTTLE (INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE)
Survey data indicates that the "last-mile" transit gap between Kurla/Chembur railway stations and the campus gate historically forced over 1,200 students daily into fossil-fueled three-wheeler auto-rickshaws.
To resolve this, the college commissioned project INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE in January 2024, operating two dedicated 14-seater Mahindra Supro electric vans. In its initial 10 months of operation:
- Completed over 1,800 scheduled shuttle trips.
- Transported 38,400 passenger-trips.
- Consumed 4,464 kWh of electricity, charged on-campus using solar power from BLD_ACA.
- Displaced fossil-fuel auto-rickshaw journeys, abating 36,000 kg CO2e net.

5. STRATEGIC INTERVENTIONS TO MEET TARGET TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE
Baseline clean commuting share (train + bus + walking/cycling) stands at 52.0%. To achieve the 70.0% clean commute mandate by 2027 under TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE, the survey committee recommends:
- Procuring two 24-passenger electric mini-buses to expand INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE frequency.
- Installing 20 secure bicycle lockers and shower stations in BLD_ACA.
- Launching an AI-enabled carpool coordination module within the campus mobile portal.

title: IoT Smart Energy Metering and Real-Time Building Telemetry Report
content:
IOT SMART ENERGY METERING AND REAL-TIME BUILDING TELEMETRY REPORT
Document Reference: VESIT/TECH/IOT-ENERGY/2024/01
Project Reference: INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT (Campus IoT Energy Management)
Executing Departments: Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN) and Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. ARCHITECTURAL TOPOLOGY AND HARDWARE DEPLOYMENT
In March 2024, Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) deployed project INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT, a campus-wide digital telemetry network designed to provide granular, continuous monitoring of electrical energy flows. The infrastructure covers 32,500 m2 of institutional floor space across seven buildings: Academic Block A (BLD_ACA), Academic Block B (BLD_ACB), Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB), Library (BLD_LIB), Auditorium (BLD_AUD), Canteen (BLD_CAN), and Administration Block (BLD_ADM).

The deployment comprises 45 industrial multi-function digital energy meters (Schneider Electric EM6400NG series) communicating over RS-485 serial buses using the open Modbus-RTU protocol. Meters are integrated across all Main Distribution Boards (MDBs) and Sub-Distribution Boards (SDBs). Five edge gateway nodes (Raspberry Pi 4 Compute Modules running industrial Linux) query the meter network every 15 seconds, aggregating active power (kW), reactive power (kVAR), line voltage (V), phase current (A), total harmonic distortion (THD), and power factor (PF). Normalized telemetry is packaged into lightweight JSON payloads and published via MQTT over the campus fiber-optic backbone to a secure local time-series server running InfluxDB and Grafana, mirrored directly into the EcoClock AI knowledge engine.

2. TELEMETRY INSIGHTS AND ANOMALOUS CONSUMPTION DISCOVERY
Analysis of over 18 million continuous telemetry records collected between April 1 and September 30, 2024, uncovered three substantial operational inefficiencies:
2.1 Computer Laboratories Standby Baselines (BLD_LAB):
Telemetry established that non-operational nighttime electrical draw (between 22:00 and 06:00) averaged 24.2 kW. Despite labs being unoccupied, over 380 desktop PC workstation power supplies remained plugged in quiescent sleep mode, drawing 18-22 W each. Concurrently, precision air conditioning units in server rooms were operating at sub-optimal setpoints of 19.0°C instead of the recommended 24.0°C.
2.2 Auditorium Parasitic Loads (BLD_AUD):
In the Auditorium, stage lighting step-down transformers, audio power amplifiers, and projection cooling fans drew 3.8 kW continuous parasitic power even when the hall was dark and locked between weekly events.
2.3 Academic Concurrency Demand Spikes (BLD_ACA and BLD_ACB):
Campus peak demand reached 410 kW between 11:30 and 14:00 on weekdays, caused by simultaneous operation of heavy lab computing, classroom split ACs, and Canteen kitchen ventilation.

3. AUTOMATED CONTROL INTERVENTIONS AND QUANTIFIED ENERGY CONSERVATION
To eliminate these identified baseload drains, the engineering team executed three firmware and control optimizations:
- Smart Contactor Bench Relays: Installed 16 automated Modbus-controlled relay banks across BLD_LAB. Timed firmware scripts automatically disconnect electrical supply to student workstation benches at 20:30 on weekdays and all weekend hours, eliminating 16.5 kW of phantom draw.
- Server Room Climate Optimization: Reprogrammed precision CRAC thermostats in the AI Research server room from 19.0°C to 24.0°C, delivering an immediate 14.2% reduction in compressor energy demand without compromising hardware thermal margins.
- Occupancy Automation in BLD_AUD: Integrated passive infrared (PIR) occupancy sensors to de-energize stage lighting transformers when the hall is vacant for over 15 minutes.

4. ENERGY AND CARBON REDUCTION IMPACT
Post-optimization telemetry over a verified 90-day period demonstrated a sustained 4.80% reduction in campus-wide monthly electricity consumption:
- Annualized Electricity Conservation: 98,000 kWh saved across campus facilities.
- Avoided Grid Emissions: Applying Central Electricity Authority factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh), the IoT project directly abated 80,360 kg CO2e in 2024.
- Financial Return: Annual utility bill reductions equal INR 10,78,000 against a total IoT implementation expenditure of INR 8,40,000, establishing a simple payback period of only 9.3 months.
The telemetry infrastructure directly underpins target TRG_NET_ZERO and advances United Nations SDG 7, SDG 9, and SDG 12.

title: Miyawaki Native Afforestation and Campus Carbon Sequestration Report
content:
MIYAWAKI NATIVE AFFORESTATION AND CAMPUS CARBON SEQUESTRATION REPORT
Document Reference: VESIT/BIO/AFFOREST/2024/01
Project Identifier: INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE (Miyawaki Native Afforestation Project)
Executing Unit: Campus Nature Club and Environmental Civil Cell.
Advisory Support: Social Forestry Division, Government of Maharashtra.
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. BOTANICAL PROJECT GENESIS AND METHODOLOGY
In June 2023, Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) dedicated a 600 m2 peripheral parcel of land located immediately south of the Auditorium building (BLD_AUD) to establish a high-density native micro-forest. The project deployed the internationally recognized Miyawaki afforestation methodology pioneered by Japanese botanist Dr. Akira Miyawaki. This ecological technique mimics natural forest succession by planting indigenous multi-canopy trees at high density (3 to 4 saplings per square meter), stimulating rapid upward growth through competitive sunlight seeking and accelerated root mycorrhizal networks.

Soil preparation involved excavating topsoil to a depth of 1.0 meter, incorporating organic perforated amendments: 4,000 kg of composted bioslurry produced on-campus by the Canteen anaerobic digester (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN), coco-peat for moisture retention, rice husk for aeration, and indigenous micro-organisms. A total of 1,200 saplings across 32 indigenous tree and shrub species native to the Northern Western Ghats and Konkan coastal ecosystem were planted in July 2023.

2. SPECIES COMPOSITION AND MULTI-LAYER CANOPY STRATIFICATION
The botanical inventory was organized across four structural canopy tiers:
- Canopy Emergent Trees (Overstory, 15-20m potential height): Ficus religiosa (Peepal), Ficus benghalensis (Banyan), Azadirachta indica (Neem), Syzygium cumini (Jamun), and Mangifera indica (Native Mango).
- Sub-Canopy Trees (10-15m): Pongamia pinnata (Karanj), Bauhinia variegata (Kanchan), Cassia fistula (Amaltas), and Alstonia scholaris (Saptaparni).
- Understory Small Trees & Large Shrubs (5-10m): Morinda citrifolia (Noni), Phyllanthus emblica (Amla), and Bambusa multiplex (Hedge Bamboo).
- Ground Cover & Medicinal Shrubs: Adhatoda vasica (Adulsa), Ocimum sanctum (Tulsi), and Rauvolfia serpentina (Sarpagandha).

3. ECOLOGICAL SURVIVAL METRICS AND MICROCLIMATIC IMPACTS
At the comprehensive 12-month ecological audit completed in June 2024:
- Survival Rate: Recorded an exceptional 94.2% survival rate (1,130 surviving trees out of 1,200 planted), attributed to drip irrigation utilizing treated canteen greywater and rainwater cistern supplies from INIT_RWH_SYSTEM.
- Canopy Growth: Average canopy height surpassed 3.8 meters, with pioneer species (Karanj and Bamboo) exceeding 5.2 meters. Canopy foliage density has created a closed-canopy micro-ecosystem.
- Biodiversity Index: Avian and pollinator surveys conducted by student volunteers documented 24 resident and migratory bird species (including oriental magpie robins, sunbirds, and coppersmith barbets) alongside 18 butterfly species.
- Microclimate Cooling: Thermal infrared sensor arrays deployed under INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT measured a localized ambient temperature depression of 2.3°C within the forest interior compared to adjacent paved asphalt parking surfaces, significantly mitigating the local urban heat island phenomenon.

4. ALLOMETRIC BIOMASS AND CARBON SEQUESTRATION MODELING
Carbon sequestration was quantified using standard non-destructive allometric biomass equations developed by the Forest Survey of India (FSI) for tropical broadleaf species:
Biomass (kg) = 0.0509 * (Diameter at Breast Height in cm)^2 * Height (m) * Wood Density
- Current Measured Sequestration (Year 1): 14,000 kg CO2e/year (14.0 metric tonnes CO2e).
- Projected Maturity Sequestration (Year 5 - 2028): 26,500 kg CO2e/year.
- Projected Climax Sequestration (Year 10 - 2033): 38,000 kg CO2e/year.

The project contributes tangible biotic carbon removal advancing target TRG_NET_ZERO, directly supporting United Nations SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 15 (Life on Land). Future plans incorporate expanding the afforestation corridor by an additional 400 m2 along the eastern campus perimeter.

title: Building Energy Benchmark: Computer Laboratories High-Density Compute Audit
content:
BUILDING ENERGY BENCHMARK: COMPUTER LABORATORIES HIGH-DENSITY COMPUTE AUDIT
Document Reference: VESIT/BMK/LAB-ENERGY/2024/01
Facility Code: BLD_LAB (Computer Laboratories Building)
Departmental Jurisdiction: Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN) and Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. FACILITY ARCHITECTURE AND COMPUTE ASSET INVENTORY
The Computer Laboratories building (BLD_LAB) encompasses 5,200 m2 of specialized academic floor area across four levels. The facility accommodates over 650 concurrent students and faculty, housing 16 dedicated departmental computer laboratories, two enterprise server rooms, and an Advanced AI & High-Performance Computing Research Center. Compute infrastructure includes 680 desktop workstations, 12 GPU-accelerated machine learning workstation towers (NVIDIA RTX A6000 clusters), and two enterprise server rack cabinets running round-the-clock academic services, repository mirrors, and campus AI workloads.

2. ENERGY CONSUMPTION ANALYSIS AND BENCHMARK DISPARITY
In calendar year 2024, facility sub-metering under project INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT registered a gross annual electricity consumption of 582,400 kWh for BLD_LAB. Despite representing only 16.0% of the institution's total built-up area (32,500 m2), the building accounts for 24.65% of total campus electrical consumption (2,362,400 kWh).
- Specific Energy Consumption (SEC): Measured at 112.0 kWh/m2/year. This is more than double the specific energy intensity of Academic Block A (BLD_ACA at 51.0 kWh/m2/year) and Academic Block B (BLD_ACB at 49.0 kWh/m2/year).
- Carbon Attribution: At regional grid emission factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh), the facility generated 477,568 kg CO2e in 2024, making it the single largest point source of Scope 2 emissions on campus.

3. SUB-SYSTEM LOAD DISTRIBUTION AND LOSS ANALYSIS
Detailed power distribution monitoring identified four core consumption streams:
- IT Workstations and Compute Hardware: 44.0% (256,256 kWh/year). Lab PCs and GPU workstations draw substantial energy during daily sessions. However, 18.2% of workstation power was consumed during idle evening and weekend hours due to inactive PCs left plugged into unswitched bench outlets.
- Precision HVAC and Space Air Conditioning: 41.0% (238,784 kWh/year). Space cooling is provided by a combination of conventional split air conditioners in teaching labs and dedicated precision air handling units (PAHUs) in server rooms.
- Architectural LED Lighting: 9.0% (52,416 kWh/year).
- UPS Conversion Inefficiencies and Auxiliary Losses: 6.0% (34,944 kWh/year). Central double-conversion online UPS units operate at an average load factor of only 38%, resulting in an 11% parasitic thermal conversion loss.

4. SERVER ROOM POWER USAGE EFFECTIVENESS (PUE) AUDIT
The audit evaluated the primary AI Research Server Room housing campus computing clusters:
- Total Server Room Power Draw: 48,200 kWh/year.
- IT Equipment Compute Energy: 27,700 kWh/year.
- Server Room Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE): Calculated at 1.74 (Total Power / IT Power). A PUE of 1.74 indicates significant cooling inefficiency, well above modern green data center benchmarks (1.20 - 1.35). Inefficiencies stem from mixing hot exhaust air with cold supply air across server racks.

5. TARGETED RETROFIT ACTION PLAN
To decarbonize BLD_LAB and support institutional targets TRG_NET_ZERO and TRG_RENEWABLE:
- Cold Aisle Containment: Install physical acrylic aisle doors and ceiling baffles in the server room to prevent thermal air mixing, coupled with adjusting cooling setpoints to 24.0°C. This will reduce PUE from 1.74 to 1.32, saving 16,500 kWh annually.
- Smart Automated Workstation Relays: Program automated master circuit contactors to de-energize lab benches between 20:30 and 07:30, eliminating 32,000 kWh/year of standby draw.
- Combined Savings: 48,500 kWh/year (39,770 kg CO2e avoided), supporting United Nations SDG 7, SDG 9, and SDG 12.

title: Facility Sustainability Review: Canteen and Dining Hall Operations
content:
FACILITY SUSTAINABILITY REVIEW: CANTEEN AND DINING HALL OPERATIONS
Document Reference: VESIT/FAC/CANTEEN/2024/01
Facility Code: BLD_CAN (Canteen Building)
Jurisdiction: Canteen Oversight Committee and Campus Facilities (DEP_ADMN).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. OPERATIONAL SCOPE AND RESOURCE METRICS
The Canteen building (BLD_CAN) occupies 2,100 m2 of built infrastructure comprising an industrial commercial kitchen, two student dining halls, a faculty dining lounge, and outdoor shaded eating patios. Serving a campus community of 3,200 individuals, the facility processes over 2,200 meals, snacks, and beverages every academic working day.

Because of intensive food preparation, utensil sanitation, and catering operations, BLD_CAN represents the campus's primary hub of solid organic waste generation, high daily water consumption, and commercial cooking fuel use:
- Annual Electricity Consumption: 192,000 kWh (specific intensity: 91.4 kWh/m2/year), driven by commercial refrigeration, induction warmers, ventilation exhaust hoods, and drinking water chillers.
- Annual Municipal Water Consumption: 13,440,000 litres (28.0% of total campus freshwater intake).
- Annual Solid Organic Waste: 28,728 kg of wet vegetable peelings, uneaten food scraps, and coffee grounds.

2. ON-SITE ANAEROBIC BIOMETHANATION PLANT (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN)
To address wet food waste, the institution commissioned project INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN directly adjacent to the kitchen loading dock. The facility houses a 250 kg/day prefabricated anaerobic biomethanation reactor utilizing a microbial consortia optimized for starch, cellulose, and lipid degradation.
During 2024:
- Ingested 19,200 kg of source-segregated canteen kitchen scraps.
- Generated 4,380 m3 of methane-rich biogas (average 12.0 m3/day).
- Replaced 168 commercial LPG cylinders (19 kg each) annually, piped directly to two kitchen burners.
- Delivered direct fuel cost savings of INR 3,00,000 per year while abating 48,000 kg CO2e of fugitive methane and fossil fuel combustion emissions.
- Produced 1,400 kg of enriched liquid bioslurry and solid bio-manure utilized on campus botanical grounds.

3. SINGLE-USE PLASTIC ELIMINATION AND WASTE PACKAGING
In compliance with the Maharashtra Plastic and Thermocol Products notification and campus Circular Economy guidelines (DOC_WST_018):
- 100% Transition to Reusable Tableware: The canteen completely eliminated single-use plastic plates, bowls, cups, and polystyrene foam trays, transitioning to high-grade 304 food-grade stainless steel thali trays, copper-bottom water jugs, and ceramic cups.
- Elimination of Packaged Water Bottles: Replaced the retail sale of 500ml single-use PET bottled water with three high-capacity chilled commercial reverse osmosis (RO) bottle refill stations. This intervention eliminates over 42,000 disposable plastic bottles annually.
- Takeaway Packaging Protocol: Banned plastic takeaway wraps; all takeaway food containers are mandated to use certified biodegradable sugarcane bagasse clamshells and birchwood cutlery.

4. WATER RECOVERY AND GREYWATER CYCLING
Commercial RO purification currently discharges 14,000 litres/day of mineral-rich reject water. A plumbing retrofit currently underway routes this reject water to the dual-flush toilet tanks of BLD_CAN and the adjacent Academic Block A (BLD_ACA). Concurrently, a 15,000 L/day constructed wetland reed-bed system is scheduled for 2025 behind BLD_CAN to biologically purify greasy kitchen greywater for landscape irrigation.

These integrated canteen operations form the backbone of institutional compliance with targets TRG_ZERO_WASTE and TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL, directly demonstrating compliance with United Nations SDG 6, SDG 12, and SDG 13.

title: Facility Sustainability Review: Library Energy and Daylighting Optimization
content:
FACILITY SUSTAINABILITY REVIEW: LIBRARY ENERGY AND DAYLIGHTING OPTIMIZATION
Document Reference: VESIT/FAC/LIB-ENERGY/2024/01
Facility Code: BLD_LIB (Library Building)
Departmental Custody: Library Committee and Campus Facilities (DEP_ADMN).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. FACILITY PROFILE AND ARCHITECTURAL ATTRIBUTES
The Central Library building (BLD_LIB) encompasses 3,100 m2 of dedicated academic space spanning three levels. The building accommodates over 350 concurrent readers, featuring reading halls, periodical stacks, administrative reference desks, and an Advanced Digital Knowledge Portal equipped with 40 research terminals.

Architecturally, the building benefits from extensive floor-to-ceiling double-glazed fenestration along its eastern and northern facades, providing an abundance of natural daylight throughout morning and early afternoon hours. In 2024, the library consumed 168,200 kWh of electricity (54.2 kWh/m2/year), representing 7.12% of campus electrical consumption.

2. DAYLIGHT-HARVESTING SMART LIGHTING RETROFIT

- Photocell Dimming Automation: Installed 12 photocell daylight sensors along the eastern perimeter reading zones. The smart lighting controller continuously measures ambient lux levels, automatically dimming artificial LED illumination when natural sunlight exceeds 400 lux.
- Energy Impact: The lighting retrofit reduced connected lighting load from 14.7 kW to 5.76 kW, saving 22,400 kWh annually and abating 18,368 kg CO2e based on CEA factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh).

3. ROOFTOP SOLAR PV INTEGRATION (INIT_SOLAR_PH1)
Mounted on the terrace of BLD_LIB is a 30 kWp grid-tied monocrystalline solar photovoltaic array (75 modules of 400 Wp each) commissioned under Phase-1 Solar (INIT_SOLAR_PH1).
In 2024:

- Directly satisfied 25.33% of the building's total annual electricity demand on-site.
- Avoided 34,932 kg CO2e of Scope 2 indirect emissions.
- Generated net electricity bill savings of INR 4,68,600.

4. DIGITALIZATION AND CIRCULAR RESOURCE CONSERVATION

- Bound Print Reductions: Reduced institutional paper consumption for student project reports and syllabi by 65% since 2022, conserving an estimated 4.2 metric tonnes of paper annually.
- Avoided Embodied Emissions: Applying life-cycle paper manufacturing factors, paper digitization avoided 5,880 kg CO2e of embodied emissions.
These interventions establish BLD_LIB as a benchmark sustainable educational facility advancing SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), and SDG 13 (Climate Action), supporting target TRG_NET_ZERO.

title: Facility Sustainability Review: Auditorium HVAC and Event Load Management
