Operational Authority: Campus Events Directorate and Facilities (DEP_ADMN).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. FACILITY CHARACTERISTICS AND OCCUPANCY PROFILE
The Campus Auditorium (BLD_AUD) encompasses 2,800 m2 of built infrastructure featuring an 800-seat multi-tier main auditorium, stage wing facilities, sound engineering booths, green rooms, and a spacious pre-function entrance foyer. The building hosts major institutional milestone events, technical symposia, national conferences, cultural festivals, and placement drives.

Unlike standard academic classrooms that maintain predictable weekday schedules, BLD_AUD exhibits an intermittent high-demand electrical load profile. During major technical symposiums or full-capacity conferences, instantaneous cooling and lighting power demand surges up to 180 kW. However, the facility remains unoccupied for approximately 65% of standard calendar weekdays, creating acute operational challenges in energy management.

2. ENERGY CONSUMPTION ANALYSIS AND HVAC DYNAMICS
In 2024, BLD_AUD consumed 134,200 kWh of grid electricity (47.9 kWh/m2/year), resulting in 110,044 kg CO2e of Scope 2 emissions based on CEA emission factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh):
- Space Air Conditioning: Accounts for 72.0% of total building consumption (96,624 kWh/year). Space cooling is provided by two 70-ton packaged water-cooled chillers (total 140 TR capacity).
- Stage Lighting and Audio-Visual Electronics: 18.0% (24,156 kWh/year).
- Auxiliary Motors, Ventilation Fans, and Foyers: 10.0% (13,420 kWh/year).

Prior to deploying IoT sub-metering under INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT in March 2024, telemetry logs revealed that facility staff frequently initiated chiller pull-down cycles five to six hours before rehearsals, running chillers across vacant halls. Furthermore, high-power stage lighting transformers drew 3.8 kW continuous standby power even during days of complete building closure.

3. OPERATIONAL OPTIMIZATIONS IMPLEMENTED
To eliminate wasted energy, the facilities team deployed three control protocols:
- Occupancy-Linked HVAC Pre-Cooling Algorithm: Implemented an automated control schedule calibrated to indoor wet-bulb temperatures. Pre-cooling is strictly limited to 45 minutes prior to hall occupancy, utilizing variable frequency drives (VFDs) on air-handling units to modulate airflow based on real-time CO2 ppm levels.
- Automated Standby Contactor Isolation: Programmable relays now fully disconnect stage lighting transformer substations when the master auditorium lighting console is powered off.
- Quantified Energy Conservation: These operational changes achieved a measured 16.4% reduction in building consumption, saving 22,000 kWh annually (18,040 kg CO2e avoided).

4. PROPOSED 50 KWP SOLAR BIFACIAL RETROFIT (INIT_SOLAR_PH2)
The Auditorium possesses an unobstructed curved perimeter roof covering 1,200 m2. Phase-2 solar feasibility modeling (DOC_ENG_004) proposes installing 50 kWp of lightweight bifacial photovoltaic modules on this roof. The installation will generate 71,000 kWh annually, satisfying over 52.9% of the Auditorium's annual electricity demand on-site and abating 58,220 kg CO2e annually, advancing institutional targets TRG_NET_ZERO and TRG_RENEWABLE while supporting SDG 7, SDG 11, and SDG 13.

title: Campus Commuting Decarbonisation: Electric Shuttle Route Optimization Study
content:
CAMPUS COMMUTING DECARBONISATION: ELECTRIC SHUTTLE ROUTE OPTIMIZATION STUDY
Document Reference: VESIT/MOB/SHUTTLE/2024/02
Project Code: INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE (Zero-Emission Electric Campus Transit)
Executing Department: Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS) and Campus Administration (DEP_ADMN).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. CONTEXT AND LAST-MILE TRANSIT BOTTLENECK
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) in Chembur, Mumbai, accommodates a commuter community of 3,200 individuals. Mobility surveys (DOC_TRN_007) confirmed that 48.0% of students and staff utilize Mumbai's suburban rail network, arriving at Chembur and Tilak Nagar stations (Harbour Line) or Kurla station (Central Line). However, the remaining 2.4 km distance between these stations and the campus gate historically constituted a severe last-mile transit bottleneck. Over 1,200 commuters daily relied on fossil-fueled three-wheeler auto-rickshaws, generating congestion and substantial localized air pollutants.

To solve this challenge and advance institutional target TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE (70.0% low-carbon commuting by 2027), the college chartered initiative INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE, procuring two dedicated electric passenger vans in January 2024.

2. FLEET SPECIFICATIONS AND SMART SOLAR CHARGING REGIME
The transit fleet comprises two commercial Mahindra Supro EV passenger vans:
- Seating Capacity: 14 passengers + 1 driver.
- Powertrain: 48V AC induction electric traction motor delivering 19.5 kW peak power and 58 Nm torque.
- Battery Pack: 20.0 kWh lithium-ion battery system delivering a verified real-world operational range of 115 km per full charge.
- On-Campus Solar Charging Protocol: Vans recharge at two dedicated 7.4 kW Level-2 AC smart EV charging stations installed in the central parking lot. Charging schedules are coordinated through smart controllers to draw power between 11:00 and 15:00 on weekdays, directly capturing peak rooftop solar photovoltaic generation from Academic Block A (BLD_ACA, INIT_SOLAR_PH1). This guarantees that the shuttle fleet runs on 100% clean, zero-emissions electricity.

3. TEN-MONTH OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE EVALUATION (JAN - OCT 2024)
Fleet telematics and ticketing logs over the initial 10-month service window established:
- Total Distance Traveled: 24,800 fleet kilometres across Chembur and Kurla feeder routes.
- Commuter Trips Delivered: 38,400 passenger-trips.
- Fleet Energy Consumption: 4,464 kWh of electricity consumed (average fleet efficiency: 0.18 kWh/km).
- Operational Route Reliability: 98.4% on-time departure rate during peak morning (07:45 to 10:30) and evening (16:00 to 18:30) academic rush hours.

4. CARBON EMISSIONS ABATEMENT MODELING
Carbon abatement was modeled by calculating displaced passenger-kilometres against the baseline fossil fuel fleet:
- Baseline Displaced Modes: Displaced trips predominantly substituted shared three-wheeler petrol/CNG auto-rickshaws (emission factor: 0.082 kg CO2e/passenger-km) and private two-wheelers (EF_TRANS_BIKE = 0.042 kg CO2e/passenger-km).
- Gross Avoided Emissions: Displacing 92,160 passenger-km of three-wheeler transit prevented 7,557 kg CO2e; displacing 61,440 passenger-km of two-wheeler transit avoided 2,580 kg CO2e.
- Modal Substitution & Traffic Decongestion: Fleet routing prevented private vehicle idling at the campus gate, yielding an aggregate verified net carbon savings of 36,000 kg CO2e in 2024.

5. FLEET EXPANSION AND CAPACITY RECOMMENDATIONS
Passenger demand consistently exceeds current capacity during morning peak hours (average load factor: 104%, with student queues at Kurla station). The study recommends:
- Procuring two 24-seater electric mini-buses by Q2 2025 under Phase 2 transit planning.
- Tripling daily passenger throughput to 115,000 passenger-trips annually.
- Expanding avoided emissions to 95,000 kg CO2e/year, guaranteeing complete fulfillment of TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE and advancing United Nations SDG 11 and SDG 13.

title: Rainwater Harvesting Hydrological Yield and Recharge Assessment 2024
content:
RAINWATER HARVESTING HYDROLOGICAL YIELD AND RECHARGE ASSESSMENT 2024
Document Reference: VESIT/HYD/RWH-AUDIT/2024/01
Project Reference: INIT_RWH_SYSTEM (Integrated Rainwater Harvesting and Recharge)
Consulting Authority: AquaTerra Environmental Hydrology in association with VESIT Campus Infrastructure Cell.
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. HYDROLOGICAL CATCHMENT CHARACTERIZATION
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) in Chembur, Mumbai, occupies an urban plot with 32,500 m2 of built-up footprint. During the 2024 southwest monsoon season (June 1 to September 30), the regional meteorological station in Chembur recorded a cumulative seasonal rainfall of 2,420 mm.

The campus integrated rainwater harvesting system (INIT_RWH_SYSTEM) evaluates two distinct hydrological catchment surfaces:
- Terrace Rooftop Catchment: 18,000 m2 of reinforced cement concrete (RCC) terrace roofs across Academic Block A (BLD_ACA, 5,500 m2 effective catchment), Academic Block B (BLD_ACB, 5,200 m2 effective), Library (BLD_LIB, 2,800 m2), and Administration Block (BLD_ADM, 4,500 m2). All roof surfaces feature food-grade elastomeric waterproofing membranes and stainless steel wire debris mesh.
- Interlocking Paver Ground Catchment: 4,200 m2 of heavy-duty permeable concrete pavers across primary pedestrian walkways and plazas.

2. RUNOFF POTENTIAL AND MASS BALANCE MODELING
Theoretical harvestable precipitation was determined using the rational hydrological formula:
Annual Yield Potential (Q) = Area (A) * Precipitation (P) * Runoff Coefficient (C)
- Rooftop Catchment Potential: 18,000 m2 * 2.420 m * 0.85 (concrete terrace runoff coefficient) = 37,026,000 litres (37,026 m3).
- Permeable Paver Ground Potential: 4,200 m2 * 2.420 m * 0.70 (permeable paver runoff coefficient) = 7,114,800 litres (7,115 m3).
Total seasonal harvestable potential across campus surfaces reached 44,140,800 litres.

3. PHYSICAL HARVESTING INFRASTRUCTURE AND DIRECT UTILITY DISPLACEMENT
Physical infrastructure constraints dictate how harvested precipitation is routed:
- Terrace Filtration and Cistern Storage: Runoff from the 18,000 m2 rooftop catchments is directed through four centrifugal vortex leaf filters and twin rapid gravity sand-gravel bed filters (media depth: 1.2 m graded quartz sand and quartz pebbles) into three interconnected underground reinforced concrete cisterns with a total static storage capacity of 450,000 litres.
- Directly Captured and Utilized Volume: In 2024, the storage cisterns harvested, filtered, and delivered 12,400,000 litres of clean water into the non-potable overhead distribution network of BLD_ACA and BLD_ACB. This water supplied dual-flush toilets, janitorial floor scrubbing, and cooling tower makeup, directly replacing 25.83% of the campus's annual municipal freshwater demand (48,000,000 litres).
- Deep Aquifer Recharge Borewells: The remaining surplus terrace and paver runoff (31,740,800 litres) exceeded cistern capacity and was directed into four deep injection borewells (drilled to depths of 45-60 meters into basaltic fissured rock). The recharge system features desilting filtration pits that direct clean storm runoff into the subterranean water table, counteracting seawater intrusion and maintaining local groundwater reserves.

4. LABORATORY WATER QUALITY TESTING
Comprehensive water quality analysis was conducted in August 2024 at an accredited environmental laboratory. Filtered cistern water registered:
- pH: 7.2 (acceptable range: 6.5 - 8.5).
- Total Dissolved Solids (TDS): 84 mg/L (benchmark limit: 500 mg/L).
- Turbidity: 1.8 NTU (benchmark limit: 5 NTU).
- Total Coliform Bacteria: Absent (zero colonies/100ml after inline UV disinfection).
Testing confirms complete compliance with Bureau of Indian Standards BIS 10500 non-potable institutional recycling criteria.

5. CONTRIBUTION TO TARGET TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL
The verified 12.4 million litres of captured water provides critical operational progress toward target TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL (30% municipal water reduction by 2029). Expanding cistern capacity by 200,000 litres is recommended to capture an additional 4,500,000 litres annually, advancing United Nations SDG 6, SDG 11, and SDG 12.

title: VESIT Climate Action Roadmap 2024-2040: Net-Zero Trajectory Modeling
content:
VESIT CLIMATE ACTION ROADMAP 2024-2040: NET-ZERO TRAJECTORY MODELING
Document Reference: VESIT/PLN/NETZERO-ROADMAP/2024/V1
Authoring Body: Campus Decarbonization Working Group and Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS).
Institutional Target: TRG_NET_ZERO (Net-Zero GHG Emissions by December 31, 2040)
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. STATUTORY CHARTER AND BASELINE REFERENCE
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) in Chembur, Mumbai, adopts this binding Climate Action Roadmap to systematically steer institutional capital investments, facilities modernization, and operational policies toward absolute net-zero operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by December 31, 2040. The roadmap encompasses all academic and administrative facilities across 32,500 m2 of built infrastructure.

The comprehensive calendar year 2024 baseline audit (DOC_AUD_002) established the verified institutional carbon footprint:
- Total Baseline Emissions (E0): 2,450,000 kg CO2e/year (2,450 metric tonnes CO2e).
- Scope 1 Direct Emissions: 49,312 kg CO2e (2.01%), driven by 18,400 L of diesel combustion in emergency generators (EF_DIESEL_GEN = 2.68 kg CO2e/L).
- Scope 2 Indirect Imported Electricity Emissions: 1,681,000 kg CO2e (68.61%), resulting from 2,050,000 kWh of grid electricity purchase (EF_ELEC_GRID = 0.82 kg CO2e/kWh).
- Scope 3 Commuting, Waste, and Water Emissions: 719,688 kg CO2e (29.38%), comprising commuter transit (580,000 kg CO2e), municipal landfill waste (115,000 kg CO2e), and water processing (24,688 kg CO2e).

2. MATHEMATICAL DECARBONIZATION TRAJECTORY MODELING
To achieve net zero over the 16-year operational horizon (t0 = 2024 to t_target = 2040), the Department of AI & Data Science (DEP_AIDS) developed two mathematical trajectories:
2.1 Model A: Linear Decarbonization Trajectory (Constant Annual Abatement)
E_linear(t) = E0 - r * (t - t0)
Where:
- E0 = 2,450,000 kg CO2e
- Planning Horizon = 16 years
- Required Annual Linear Abatement Rate: r = 2,450,000 / 16 = 153,125 kg CO2e/year.
Under this trajectory, emissions must decrease to:
- 1,990,625 kg CO2e by 2027
- 1,531,250 kg CO2e by 2030
- 765,625 kg CO2e by 2035
- Exactly 0 kg CO2e by December 31, 2040.
2.2 Model B: Compound Annual Reduction Trajectory (Exponential Decay)
E_compound(t) = E0 * (1 - p)^(t - t0)
Requiring residual emissions by 2040 to remain below 2.0% of baseline (< 49,000 kg CO2e), the required compound abatement rate is p = 22.8% per annum if relying strictly on operational abatement, or p = 12.5% per annum when coupled with high-integrity local biological sequestration (INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE).

The Taskforce adopts Model A (Linear Decarbonization) as the statutory institutional compliance benchmark, reviewed quarterly on the EcoClock AI interactive platform.

3. THREE-PHASE IMPLEMENTATION MILESTONES
- Phase I (Immediate Execution, 2024 - 2027): Focuses on low-hanging energy efficiency and on-site generation. Commission Phase-2 Solar (INIT_SOLAR_PH2, 200 kWp + 100 kWh BESS) across parking lots and BLD_AUD, cutting 232,880 kg CO2e. Expand INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE to four electric vans, abating 95,000 kg CO2e. Enforce IoT thermostat lockdowns (INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT), saving 80,360 kg CO2e. Full canteen food waste biomethanation (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN), abating 48,000 kg CO2e. Phase 1 cumulative annual abatement: 456,240 kg CO2e/year.
- Phase II (Deep Institutional Transformation, 2028 - 2032): Execute green power wheeling agreements (1.2 MW off-site group captive solar-wind farm under open access regulations) to displace remaining imported grid electricity, eliminating 1,150,000 kg CO2e. Expand rainwater harvesting cisterns to 650,000 L and mandate fleet electrification for all contracted campus staff buses.
- Phase III (Residual Decarbonization and Sequestration, 2033 - 2040): Transition all HVAC chillers to ultra-low GWP refrigerants (R-1234ze / R-290). Mature biomass growth across the expanded Miyawaki forest (INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE) sequesters 38,000 kg CO2e/year, neutralizing residual operational emissions to achieve absolute Net-Zero by December 31, 2040.

4. MONITORING AND VERIFICATION GOVERNANCE
Progress shall be continuously tracked using the EcoClock AI GraphRAG analytics engine, connecting utility telemetry directly to Neo4j knowledge graphs to guarantee evidence-grounded accountability advancing United Nations SDG 7, SDG 11, SDG 12, and SDG 13.

title: Campus Circular Economy and Zero-Waste Policy Guidelines
content:
CAMPUS CIRCULAR ECONOMY AND ZERO-WASTE POLICY GUIDELINES
Document Reference: VESIT/POL/CIRCULAR-WASTE/2024/V1
Promulgated by: Campus Environmental Cell and Directorate of Facilities (DEP_ADMN).
Institutional Policy Target: TRG_ZERO_WASTE (Zero Waste to Landfill & 85% Recycling by 2028).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. STATUTORY RATIONALE AND POLICY GOALS
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) in Chembur, Mumbai, adopts these Circular Economy and Zero-Waste Guidelines to eliminate the generation of unsegregated solid refuse across its 32,500 m2 built estate. Serving a population of 3,200 students, faculty, and administrative staff, the college generated 68,400 kg of solid waste in 2024. Under baseline conditions, sending unsegregated municipal solid waste to Deonar landfill results in severe greenhouse gas emissions (EF_WASTE_LANDFILL = 1.25 kg CO2e/kg waste) and regional environmental contamination.

This policy establishes strict institutional mandates to divert 85.0% of solid waste from landfills by December 31, 2028 (TRG_ZERO_WASTE), supporting United Nations SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

2. MANDATORY FOUR-STREAM SOURCE SEGREGATION PROTOCOL
Effective September 1, 2024, all academic departments—Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN), Information Technology (DEP_INFT), Electronics & Telecommunication (DEP_EXTC), AI & Data Science (DEP_AIDS), and Facilities (DEP_ADMN)—must maintain color-coded four-stream sorting receptacles at every corridor intersection, classroom block, and laboratory:
- Green Receptacle (Biodegradable Organics): Exclusively for wet food scraps, tea leaves, fruit peels, and floral waste from Canteen (BLD_CAN) and departmental lounges. Strictly zero plastic packaging. All green-bin contents are routed directly to the on-site anaerobic biomethanation plant and composting tumblers under project INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN.
- Blue Receptacle (Clean Dry Paper & Cardboard): Reserved for examination booklets, discarded textbooks, stationery paper, and corrugated cardboard boxes. Paper is bundled weekly and transferred to authorized municipal recyclers, delivering avoided carbon factor credits (EF_WASTE_RECYCLE = -0.65 kg CO2e/kg waste).
- Red Receptacle (Rigid Recyclable Plastics & Metal Cans): Designated for rigid polyethylene containers, clean aluminum beverage cans, and polypropylene labware.
- Black Receptacle (Inert Refuse & Sanitary Waste): Limited to sweepings, broken glass (wrapped separately), and non-recyclable sanitary refuse collected by municipal sanitation teams.

3. TOTAL PROHIBITION ON SINGLE-USE PLASTICS
In strict adherence to Maharashtra Plastic Waste Management rules:
- Prohibited Items: Single-use plastic cutlery, polystyrene food boxes, plastic straws, disposable plastic water bottles under 500ml, plastic promotional banners, and non-biodegradable parcel packaging are banned from campus grounds.
- Enforcement: Campus security conducts random baggage screening at entry gates. Commercial food vendors operating in the Canteen (BLD_CAN) face immediate financial penalties and contract revocation for supplying prohibited plastics.
- Alternative Mandates: Events must utilize reusable stainless steel cutlery, ceramic mugs, and certified compostable sugarcane bagasse containers.

4. SUSTAINABLE PROCUREMENT AND RECYCLED PAPER MANDATE
Institutional purchasing protocols must uphold circularity:
- Exam Paper Specifications: Administrative procurement must mandate that 100% of student semester examination answer booklets, lab journals, and administrative office stationery contain a minimum of 70% post-consumer recycled paper fiber.
- E-Waste Stewardship: Decommissioned computing hardware, monitors, and circuit boards from Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB) must undergo formal material reclamation through certified e-waste partner Greenscape Solutions under E-Waste Rules 2022, ensuring complete recovery of copper, gold, and aluminum without landfill disposal.

Quarterly waste diversion audits published via the EcoClock AI dashboard shall verify departmental compliance against target TRG_ZERO_WASTE.

title: HVAC and Chiller Plant Energy Efficiency Audit across Academic Blocks
content:
HVAC AND CHILLER PLANT ENERGY EFFICIENCY AUDIT ACROSS ACADEMIC BLOCKS
Document Reference: VESIT/AUD/HVAC-ENERGY/2024/01
Conducting Authority: Thermal Energy Systems Research Lab in collaboration with External BEE-Accredited Energy Auditors.
Scope: Academic Block A (BLD_ACA), Academic Block B (BLD_ACB), and Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB).
Location: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. EXECUTIVE CONTEXT AND COOLING ENERGY INVENTORY
Space air conditioning and ventilation represent the single largest operational electricity load at Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), accounting for 38.4% (907,160 kWh) of the total annual campus electricity consumption (2,362,400 kWh) in 2024. Operating in Mumbai's hot and humid tropical coastal climate, space cooling is critical for maintaining thermal comfort and equipment reliability across 32,500 m2 of institutional floor space.

This engineering audit evaluated cooling equipment across the primary academic blocks:
- Academic Block A (BLD_ACA, 7,500 m2): 74 split and multi-split AC units (cooling capacity: 135 TR).
- Academic Block B (BLD_ACB, 6,800 m2): 62 split AC units and ductable units (cooling capacity: 118 TR).
- Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB, 5,200 m2): Variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems and precision cooling units serving 16 computer labs and two server rooms (total capacity: 160 TR).

2. AUDIT FINDINGS AND OPERATIONAL INEFFICIENCIES
Detailed data logging across 240 operating hours revealed major efficiency bottlenecks:
- Sub-Optimal Operating Temperature Setpoints: Over 62% of faculty cabins and computer labs maintained thermostat setpoints between 19.0°C and 20.0°C, significantly below the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) recommended default comfort setpoint of 24.0°C. Controlled thermal testing confirmed that every 1.0°C increase in thermostat setpoint yields a measured 6.0% reduction in compressor electricity consumption.
- Condenser Coil Fouling and Particulate Accumulation: Ambient particulate matter in Chembur caused severe dust fouling on outdoor condenser coils of 14 split AC units in BLD_ACA, causing an 18.2% degradation in the equipment's Coefficient of Performance (COP) and forcing compressors to run continuously.
- Refrigerant GWP Profiles: 45 legacy split AC units continue to operate using HCFC-22 (R-22) refrigerant, which possesses a high Global Warming Potential (GWP of 1,810) and ozone-depleting properties.

3. MANDATED ACTION PLAN AND CONTROL MEASURES
The audit mandates four immediate engineering and policy interventions:
3.1 Mandatory Thermostat Lock at 24.0°C:
Effective August 1, 2024, all air conditioning thermostats across administrative offices, lecture halls, and faculty rooms were locked at 24.0°C via tamper-proof physical covers and digital central VRF controllers. Raising average operating setpoints from 20.0°C to 24.0°C yields an immediate 24.0% reduction in cooling energy draw.
3.2 Rigorous Preventative Maintenance Schedule:
Mandate bi-monthly chemical cleaning and pressure-washing of outdoor condenser coils using harvested rainwater from INIT_RWH_SYSTEM, restoring original manufacturer COP ratings.
3.3 Phase-Out of R-22 Refrigerants:
Establish a rolling procurement schedule to retire aging R-22 air conditioners by 2026, transitioning to high-efficiency inverter units utilizing low-GWP refrigerants: R-32 (GWP 675) for split units and R-290 propane (GWP 3) for specialized pilot lab applications.

4. ENERGY CONSERVATION AND CARBON ABATEMENT IMPACT
Full execution of the HVAC action plan will achieve:
- Annual Electricity Savings: 142,000 kWh/year across BLD_ACA, BLD_ACB, and BLD_LAB.
- Carbon Emissions Avoided: Applying Central Electricity Authority factor EF_ELEC_GRID (0.82 kg CO2e/kWh), the intervention eliminates 116,440 kg CO2e annually.
- Utility Bill Savings: INR 15,62,000 annually against an implementation cost of INR 3,80,000, achieving a payback period of only 2.9 months.
These results advance institutional targets TRG_NET_ZERO and TRG_RENEWABLE while supporting United Nations SDG 7, SDG 11, and SDG 13.

- Solid Waste Diversion Rate: 48.2% diverted from landfills via on-site composting (19,200 kg) and dry recycling (19,800 kg).
- Low-Carbon Commuter Share: 52.0% of trips delivered by train, municipal bus, EV shuttle, and cycling.

2. DETAILED PROGRESS AGAINST STATUTORY SUSTAINABILITY TARGETS
- Target Net-Zero (TRG_NET_ZERO): Decarbonize baseline 2,450,000 kg CO2e to net-zero by 2040. In Progress. The linear abatement trajectory mandates eliminating 153,125 kg CO2e annually. First-year initiatives achieved 256,168 kg CO2e of avoided solar emissions and 36,000 kg CO2e of transport abatement, exceeding year-one milestones.
- Target Renewable Electricity (TRG_RENEWABLE): Attain 50.0% clean power by 2030. In Progress. Phase-1 Solar (INIT_SOLAR_PH1, 220 kWp) generates 312,400 kWh/year. Board clearance for Phase-2 Solar (INIT_SOLAR_PH2, 200 kWp + 100 kWh BESS) will escalate clean energy generation to 596,400 kWh/year (25.25% penetration).
- Target Zero Waste to Landfill (TRG_ZERO_WASTE): Achieve 85.0% landfill diversion by 2028. In Progress. 48.2% diversion achieved in 2024 via Canteen biogas digester (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN) and paper recycling.
- Target Water Neutrality (TRG_WATER_NEUTRAL): Reduce municipal water intake by 30.0% by 2029. In Progress. 12.4 million litres harvested via INIT_RWH_SYSTEM; plumbing aerator retrofits initiated across 140 washrooms.
- Target Green Commuting (TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE): Achieve 70.0% low-carbon commuting by 2027. In Progress. Two Mahindra Supro electric vans (INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE) delivered 38,400 clean passenger-trips.

3. RESEARCH INNOVATION: THE ECOCLOCK AI PLATFORM
A primary institutional highlight was the joint development and deployment of the EcoClock AI platform by the Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN) and Department of AI & Data Science (DEP_AIDS). EcoClock AI integrates persistent Neo4j knowledge graphs, IoT telemetry from 45 Modbus smart meters (INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT), and local Mistral LLM reasoning to deliver complete transparency, interactive scenario simulation, and evidence-grounded verification. The Governing Board commends all academic departments, faculty, and student ambassadors for their pioneering environmental leadership.

title: GraphRAG for Educational Campus Decarbonization: Methodology and Architecture
content:
GRAPHRAG FOR EDUCATIONAL CAMPUS DECARBONIZATION: METHODOLOGY AND ARCHITECTURE
Document Reference: VESIT/RES/GRAPHRAG/2024/01
Authors: Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS) and Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN).
Principal Investigators: Dr. P. Sharma (DEP_AIDS) and Dr. N. Joshi (DEP_CMPN).
Institution: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai.

1. ABSTRACT AND RESEARCH MOTIVATION
Higher educational institutions worldwide are adopting ambitious institutional decarbonisation targets aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). However, verifying and communicating progress across disparate utility telemetry, unstructured policy documents, engineering audits, and complex carbon accounting frameworks remains a fundamental challenge. Conventional vector-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models rely strictly on semantic cosine similarity across isolated text chunks, frequently failing to resolve multi-hop relational dependencies—such as connecting a specific building's energy consumption (e.g., Computer Laboratories BLD_LAB) to its underlying sub-meters, parent initiatives (INIT_IOT_ENERGY_MGT), target trajectories (TRG_NET_ZERO), and corresponding UN SDGs (SDG 7, SDG 9, SDG 13).

This paper introduces the architecture and operational implementation of EcoClock AI, a hybrid Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) system engineered for Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus). The system integrates persistent Neo4j property graphs, deterministic domain ontologies, dense SentenceTransformers vector embeddings, and locally hosted large language models (Mistral-7B via Ollama) to achieve grounded, hallucination-free question answering and climate decision support.

2. GRAPH ONTOLOGY AND SCHEMA SPECIFICATION
The EcoClock AI knowledge graph formalizes campus sustainability across 16 interconnected node classes and 17 directed relationship types:
- Node Classes: Institution (VESIT), Building (BLD_ACA through BLD_ADM), Department (DEP_CMPN through DEP_ADMN), Resource (water, electricity, paper), EnergySource (grid electricity, solar PV, diesel fuel), Emission (Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3), Activity (commuting, solar generation, composting), SustainabilityInitiative (INIT_SOLAR_PH1 through INIT_BIODIVERSITY_ZONE), SustainabilityTarget (TRG_NET_ZERO through TRG_GREEN_COMMUTE), SDG (SDG_1 through SDG_17), Document (DOC_POL_001 through DOC_SMR_022), Chunk, Measurement, EmissionFactor (EF_ELEC_GRID, EF_DIESEL_GEN, etc.), ClimateScenario (linear and compound reduction), and Location (Chembur, Mumbai).
- Edge Relationships: HAS_BUILDING, HAS_DEPARTMENT, CONSUMES_RESOURCE, USES_ENERGY_SOURCE, GENERATES_EMISSION, PRODUCES_WASTE, GENERATES_MEASUREMENT, IMPLEMENTS_INITIATIVE, SUPPORTS_SDG, HAS_TARGET, ADDRESSES_TARGET, SUPPORTED_BY, HAS_CHUNK, DERIVED_FROM, APPLIES_TO, REDUCES_EMISSION, and ASSOCIATED_WITH.
Every extracted edge preserves strict provenance metadata, including source document ID, chunk ID, extraction method, confidence score, and verification status.

3. HYBRID DUAL-CHANNEL RETRIEVAL ENGINE
When a user submits a natural language query regarding institutional climate metrics, EcoClock AI executes a dual-channel hybrid retrieval pipeline:
- Channel 1 (Dense Vector Retrieval): Queries are embedded into 384-dimensional dense vectors using the BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embedding model. A cosine similarity search over chunk vectors retrieves narrative text segments with high semantic relevance.
- Channel 2 (Graph Traversal Retrieval): The query undergoes entity resolution against pre-indexed aliases (KNOWN_ALIASES). Identified entities initialize multi-hop Cypher traversals in Neo4j (depth k=2), retrieving adjacent buildings, initiatives, quantitative measurements, and SDG mappings.
- Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): Results from vector similarity and graph traversal are fused using weighted rank scoring. This guarantees that answers to complex multi-hop questions (e.g., "Which initiatives in Academic Block A address SDG 7 and what carbon reduction do they deliver?") synthesize both exact quantitative data and narrative context.

4. LLM GENERATION AND GROUNDED CITATION VERIFICATION
The fused context prompt is delivered to a locally hosted Mistral-7B-Instruct model via Ollama. The generation system prompt enforces strict evidence grounding: the LLM is prohibited from extrapolating beyond retrieved graph triples and document chunks. Answers are generated with fine-grained inline markdown citations referencing specific document IDs and chunk identifiers. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a 98.2% factual accuracy score and complete elimination of ungrounded hallucinations, establishing GraphRAG as an exemplary architecture for institutional climate transparency.

title: Comprehensive Summary: Campus Infrastructure, Buildings, and Resource Baseline

CAMPUS INFRASTRUCTURE, BUILDINGS, AND RESOURCE BASELINE REFERENCE GUIDE
Document Reference: VESIT/REF/MASTER-BASELINE/2024/V1
Authoring Directorate: Campus Decarbonization Taskforce and Facilities Management (DEP_ADMN).
Subject: Comprehensive Master Reference for Institutional Decarbonization.
Institution: Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus), Chembur, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.

1. INSTITUTIONAL METRICS AND GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION
Vivekananda Education Society's Institute of Technology (VESIT Green Campus) is an autonomous higher education engineering institution situated in the eastern suburb of Chembur, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India (Latitude: 19.0760° N, Longitude: 72.8777° E). Established on a contiguous 32,500 m2 built-up campus, the college serves 3,000 undergraduate and postgraduate engineering students, supported by 200 faculty and administrative staff members.

The campus baseline year is established as calendar year 2024, with a statutory commitment to achieve complete operational carbon neutrality (TRG_NET_ZERO) by December 31, 2040.

2. BUILDING INFRASTRUCTURE AND OCCUPANCY ASSETS
The institution comprises seven primary permanent buildings:
- Academic Block A (BLD_ACA): Built-up area 7,500 m2 | Occupancy: 1,100 | Primary use: Classrooms, tutorial halls, and faculty chambers | Housing: Department of Computer Engineering (DEP_CMPN, Head: Dr. N. Joshi) and Department of Electronics & Telecommunication (DEP_EXTC, Head: Dr. R. Kulkarni) | Solar PV installed: 80 kWp (200 modules) | 2024 Electricity: 382,500 kWh.
- Academic Block B (BLD_ACB): Area: 6,800 m2 | Occupancy: 950 | Primary use: Classrooms, seminar auditoria | Housing: Department of Information Technology (DEP_INFT, Head: Dr. S. Nair) | Solar PV: 70 kWp (175 modules) | 2024 Electricity: 333,200 kWh.
- Computer Laboratories (BLD_LAB): Area: 5,200 m2 | Occupancy: 650 | Primary use: 16 high-density computer labs, 2 primary server rooms, AI Research Center | Housing: Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (DEP_AIDS, Head: Dr. P. Sharma) | Solar PV: None (roof obstructed by cooling chillers) | 2024 Electricity: 582,400 kWh (highest intensity: 112 kWh/m2/year).
- Library (BLD_LIB): Area: 3,100 m2 | Occupancy: 350 | Primary use: Reading rooms, digital archives, stacks | Solar PV: 30 kWp (75 modules) | 2024 Electricity: 168,200 kWh.
- Auditorium (BLD_AUD): Area: 2,800 m2 | Occupancy: 800 seats | Primary use: Conferences, keynotes, cultural events | 2024 Electricity: 134,200 kWh | Proposed Phase 2 Solar: 50 kWp bifacial array.
- Canteen (BLD_CAN): Area: 2,100 m2 | Occupancy: 400 | Primary use: Food prep, dining, 2,200 daily meals | 2024 Electricity: 192,000 kWh | Annual food waste: 28,728 kg | On-site 250 kg/day biogas plant.
- Administration Block (BLD_ADM): Area: 5,000 m2 | Occupancy: 200 | Primary use: Directorate, Council Chambers, Finance, Facilities (DEP_ADMN, Head: Mr. V. Deshmukh) | Solar PV: 40 kWp (100 modules) | 2024 Electricity: 228,000 kWh.

3. RESOURCE CONSUMPTION, TELEMETRY, AND EMISSION BASELINES
3.1 Grid Electricity and Renewable Generation:
- Total Campus Electricity Consumption: 2,362,400 kWh in 2024.
- Imported Grid Electricity: 2,050,000 kWh from Maharashtra State regional grid (Emission factor EF_ELEC_GRID = 0.82 kg CO2e/kWh).
- Scope 2 Emissions: 1,681,000 kg CO2e (68.61% of campus total).
- On-Site Solar Generation (INIT_SOLAR_PH1): 312,400 kWh generated across 220 kWp rooftop arrays (BLD_ACA, BLD_ACB, BLD_LIB, BLD_ADM), delivering a 13.22% renewable electricity penetration rate and abating 256,168 kg CO2e.
3.2 Stationary Fuel and Scope 1 Emissions:
- Diesel Generator Consumption: 18,400 litres consumed during grid interruptions (Emission factor EF_DIESEL_GEN = 2.68 kg CO2e/L).
- Scope 1 Emissions: 49,312 kg CO2e (2.01% of campus total).
3.3 Water Resources and Rainwater Harvesting:
- Total Municipal Piped Water Intake: 48,000,000 litres (131,500 litres/working day).
- Rainwater Harvesting (INIT_RWH_SYSTEM): 12,400,000 litres harvested from 18,000 m2 terrace catchments and stored in 450,000 L cisterns, replacing 25.83% of municipal water needs. An additional 26,800,000 litres recharged into the local aquifer via four injection borewells.
3.4 Solid Waste and Circular Diversion:
- Total Solid Waste Generated: 68,400 kg.
- Canteen Biogas & Composting (INIT_BIOGAS_CANTEEN): 19,200 kg of food waste processed into cooking gas, abating 22,464 kg CO2e.
- Recyclables Recovered: 19,800 kg paper and 1,850 kg certified e-waste recycled with Greenscape Solutions.
- Diversion Rate: 48.2% achieved against target TRG_ZERO_WASTE (85.0% by 2028).
3.5 Transportation Mobility:
- Transportation Footprint: 580,000 kg CO2e across 3,200 commuters.
- Modal Split: Suburban Rail 48%, BEST Bus 22%, Two-Wheelers 16%, Private Cars 6%, Walking/Biking 8%.
- Campus Electric Shuttle (INIT_ELECTRIC_SHUTTLE): Two 14-seater EV vans delivered 38,400 passenger-trips, abating 36,000 kg CO2e.
3.6 Gross Baseline Emissions:
Total Calendar Year 2024 Footprint: 2,450,000 kg CO2e (2,450 metric tonnes CO2e). Target TRG_NET_ZERO mandates linear reduction of 153,125 kg CO2e annually to reach net-zero by 2040.
